title: Pyramid R-CNN: Towards Better Performance and Adaptability for 3D Object Detection
venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)

problem.summary: Current approaches generally rely on the points or voxels of interest for RoI feature extraction on the second stage, but cannot effectively handle the sparsity and non-uniform distribution of those points, and this may result in failures in detecting objects that are far away.
statements: Current approaches generally rely on the points or voxels of interest for RoI feature extraction on the second stage, but cannot effectively handle the sparsity and non-uniform distribution of those points, and this may result in failures in detecting objects that are far away.
To resolve the problems, we propose a novel second-stage module, named pyramid RoI head, to adaptively learn the features from the sparse points of interest.
Firstly, we propose the RoI-grid Pyramid, which mitigates the sparsity problem by extensively collecting points of interest for each RoI in a pyramid manner.
Our approach can mitigate the sparsity and imbalanced distribution problems of point clouds.

evidence.quote: Extensive experiments show that Pyramid R-CNN outperforms the state-of-the-art 3D detection models by a large margin on both the KITTI dataset and the Waymo Open dataset.

3) Pyramid R-CNN consistently outperforms the baselines, achieves 82.08% moderate car mAP on the KITTI dataset, and ranks 1st among the LiDAR-only methods on the Waymo test leaderboard for vehicle detection.

limitations.summary: However, the Points of Interest inevitably suffer from the sparsity and non-uniform distribution characteristics of input point clouds.
items: However, the Points of Interest inevitably suffer from the sparsity and non-uniform distribution characteristics of input point clouds.
The number of object points ranges from less than 10 to more than 500 on KITTI, and current RoI operations cannot handle the im- balanced conditions effectively.
To overcome the above limitations, we propose Pyramid R-CNN, a general two-stage 3D detection framework that can effectively detect objects and adapt along with environmental changes.
